prompt: Photorealistic naval hard-surface 3D asset modeling reference sheet for realistic World War II vessels. Absolutely realistic construction and proportions, full-scale ships, no toy aesthetic, no miniature, no low-poly stylization, no blockout geometry. Neutral light-gray background. Three rows, three views per row: detailed three-quarter view, accurate top plan view, side profile. Row 1: LCVP Higgins landing craft, curved wooden displacement hull with broad flat bow ramp, gently flared sides, believable chine transitions, thin gunwales, open troop well, sloping stern engine housing, rear steering position and paired aft machinegun posts. Row 2: 80 foot Elco PT boat, elegant narrow planing hull with bowed foredeck, rising sheer toward bow, real sloping chines, sharp entry, low faceted bridge and windshield, open cockpit, round gun tubs, deck torpedo tubes, fine railings, vents, anchor fittings, mast and stern gun position. Row 3: Fletcher-inspired destroyer, long slender curved hull with a sharp pointed bow, high forecastle deck and sheer, genuine tiered bridge with rounded corners and window bands, two thin raked funnels, open torpedo launchers amidships, five gun positions with split shield planes and exposed barrels, radar mast, boats and davits, deck machinery and finely spaced rails. Orthographic top and side views and physically believable perspective in three-quarter views. Readable gray and navy-gray painted steel surfaces with restrained material wear. Match each vessel construction across views, show every bow, stern, antenna and projecting barrel inside its cell. Use many rounded, sloped and curved surfaces with plausible structural thickness, crisp edge bevels and open recesses. Soft even studio lighting, no sea, no dramatic scenery. Favor enough large legible detail to guide rebuilding a realistic 3D model. Small labels only LCVP, ELCO PT, DESTROYER.
